speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since you had symptoms like fever and congestion eight weeks ago, did those symptoms resolve completely, or did the cough and shortness of breath start before that time?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious Bronchiolitis / Chronic Cough Variant Asthma.

The history of recent URI followed by persistent exertional and nocturnal cough is highly suggestive of post-infectious airway hyperreactivity or early asthma. Have you noticed any wheezing, chest tightness, or a history of allergies or asthma in your past?
